questions.q: When did Yahweh say the east gate of the inner courtyard would be opened?
questions.a: Yahweh said the east gate of the inner courtyard would be opened on the Sabbath and on the day of the new moon.

questions.q: Where would the prince of Israel worship?
questions.a: The prince of Israel would worship at the threshold of the inner gate.

questions.q: What would be the burnt offering of the prince on the Sabbath day?
questions.a: The prince would offer six unblemished lambs and an unblemished ram.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say was the rule about how the prince must leave after he worships?
questions.a: Yahweh said the rule was that the prince must leave by the same way he came in to worship.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say was the rule about how the people must leave after they worship?
questions.a: Yahweh said the rule was that the people must leave by going out straight ahead from where they came in.

questions.q: What would the prince have to do at a festival when he gave a freewill offering?
questions.a: The prince would have to open the east gate for the offering, and then go out and shut the gate after him.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say would be given as a burnt offering every morning?
questions.a: Yahweh said an unblemished lamb one year old would be given as a burnt offered every morning.

questions.q: According to Yahweh, who would receive the inheritance of the prince?
questions.a: The inheritance of the prince would be received by his sons.

questions.q: Why did Yahweh say the prince must not take the people’s inheritance away?
questions.a: The people’s inheritance must not be taken away so they are not scattered from their own property.

questions.q: Why were the priests not to bring the guilt, sin, and grain offerings out to the outer courtyard?
questions.a: The priests were not to bring the offerings out to the outer courtyard and so consecrate the people.

questions.q: What would be done in the cooking hearths at the corners of the outer courtyard?
questions.a: In the cooking hearths at the corners of the outer courtyard, the temple servants would boil the people’s sacrifices.

commentary.text: The ordinances of worship for the prince and for the people, are here described, and the gifts the prince may bestow on his sons and servants. Our Lord has directed us to do many duties, but he has also left many things to our choice, that those who delight in his commandments may abound therein to his glory, without entangling their own consciences, or prescribing rules unfit for others; but we must never omit our daily worship, nor neglect to apply the sacrifice of the Lamb of God to our souls, for pardon, peace, and salvation.
